name: Shechem son of Hamor
charge: Taking Dinah and defiling her; then seeking to marry into the house he had wronged and make the two peoples one
summary: Dinah, Jacob’s only daughter, went out to see the daughters of the land without supervision, and Shechem the son of Hamor, prince of the country, took her and defiled her: stranger rape, which the law sets beside murder. He did it backwards, taking first and loving after, and his father came proposing that the two peoples intermarry and become one, the offer the nations always make. Jacob’s sons answered deceitfully, and on the third day Simeon and Levi took the city with the sword.
offenseFull: Dinah went out to see the daughters of the land without supervision, and Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, took her, lay with her and defiled her (Genesis 34:1-2). That was stranger rape, and rape is a violent act; the law sets it beside murder, for as when a man rises against his neighbour and slays him, even so is this matter. The man only that lay with her shall die, and to the damsel nothing is to be done, for in her there is no sin worthy of death (Deuteronomy 22:25-27). Under it is a covetous spirit, a man desiring what is not his, which is the tenth commandment broken (Exodus 20:17). Judith remembers the act exactly: they loosened the girdle of a maid to defile her, discovered her thigh to her shame and polluted her virginity to her reproach (Judith 9:2).

The lesson stands for every generation: a man with daughters is to have a care of their body and keep a sure watch over them, for the father wakes for the daughter when no man knows, and the care for her takes away sleep, lest she be defiled and made a byword and a reproach; do not give overmuch liberty (Ecclesiasticus 7:24; Ecclesiasticus 26:10; Ecclesiasticus 42:9-11). Shechem’s soul clave to Dinah after he had defiled her; he did it backwards, taking first and loving after, which is the world’s pattern and not righteousness (Genesis 34:3). When Jacob’s sons heard it, the men were grieved and very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter, which thing ought not to be done; the laws were in place and kept long before they were written in stone at Sinai (Genesis 34:7).

Hamor proposed the exact opposite of the law: that the two houses should make marriages together, give their daughters and take his people’s daughters, dwell with them and become one people (Genesis 34:8-10, 16). Assimilation and intermarriage is the offer the nations always make, and Moses would forbid it by name (Deuteronomy 7:3). The sons of Jacob answered deceitfully, saying they could not give their sister to one that was uncircumcised, for that were a reproach to them, and requiring every male of the city to be circumcised (Genesis 34:13-15). The city’s own reasoning was written down: their cattle, their substance and every beast of Jacob’s house would be theirs (Genesis 34:23).
judgmentFull: On the third day, when they were sore, two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, came upon the city boldly and slew all the males; they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house (Genesis 34:25-26). Two men do not take a city alone. Judith says the sword of Simeon was given him of God to take vengeance of the strangers that defiled the maid, that their rulers were given to be slain and the servants smitten with their lords, and that the brothers were moved with the zeal of the Most High (Judith 9:2-4).

Jacob was troubled and said they had made him to stink among the inhabitants of the land, and feared that the nations round about would gather themselves against his house while he was few in number (Genesis 34:30). The brothers answered by asking whether he should deal with their sister as with a harlot: the daughters of Israel are not handled so, and the law allows no whore of the daughters of Israel (Genesis 34:31; Deuteronomy 23:17). His desire to marry her after the fact did not acquit him, and the marriage offer did not lessen the charge; it added to it. Jacob afterward judged the fierce anger of his sons, which is entered under their names.

text.text: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.
But if a man find a betrothed damsel in the field, and the man force her, and lie with her: then the man only that lay with her shall die:
But unto the damsel thou shalt do nothing; there is in the damsel no sin worthy of death: for as when a man riseth against his neighbour, and slayeth him, even so is this matter:
For he found her in the field, and the betrothed damsel cried, and there was none to save her.
Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.

O Lord God of my father Simeon, to whom thou gavest a sword to take vengeance of the strangers, who loosened the girdle of a maid to defile her, and discovered the thigh to her shame, and polluted her virginity to her reproach; for thou saidst, It shall not be so; and yet they did so:
Wherefore thou gavest their rulers to be slain, so that they dyed their bed in blood, being deceived, and smotest the servants with their lords, and the lords upon their thrones;

And hast given their wives for a prey, and their daughters to be captives, and all their spoils to be divided among thy dear children; which were moved with thy zeal, and abhorred the pollution of their blood, and called upon thee for aid: O God, O my God, hear me also a widow.
Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.
If thy daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly, lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty.

The father waketh for the daughter, when no man knoweth; and the care for her taketh away sleep: when she is young, lest she pass away the flower of her age; and being married, lest she should be hated:
In her virginity, lest she should be defiled and gotten with child in her father’s house; and having an husband, lest she should misbehave herself; and when she is married, lest she should be barren.

Keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies, and a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people, and make thee ashamed before the multitude.
And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.

And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.
And Hamor communed with them, saying, The soul of my son Shechem longeth for your daughter: I pray you give her him to wife.
And make ye marriages with us, and give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you.
And ye shall dwell with us: and the land shall be before you; dwell and trade ye therein, and get you possessions therein.
Then will we give our daughters unto you, and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, because he had defiled Dinah their sister:
And they said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us:
But in this will we consent unto you: If ye will be as we be, that every male of you be circumcised;
Shall not their cattle and their substance and every beast of theirs be ours? only let us consent unto them, and they will dwell with us.

And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.
And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went out.

And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and I being few in number, they shall gather themselves together against me, and slay me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.
And they said, Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?
There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.
And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.
And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.
And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel to wife.
